It's ok. The visuals are somehow both better and worse?? The sprites are worse than the original but the mansion itself looks better. The game retains all the jank that was excusable in the original game but not so much in a game that was released in 2024. Ai's story is just not enjoyable in the slightest so I can't really recommend this game at all. It's just purely OK.

There's a couple of small things altered from the original, but other than those details this game is still the same through and through. Though personally I feel like there wasn't enough added to justify the price tag, this game shouldn't cost more than $5 tops. Just go find the original and play that for free. BUT I don't regret my purchase knowing that I can support my favorite dev noprops Magic The Gathering addiction.

i'm going to be flat out when i say this. i was going in with positive expectations, but this remaster, for what it's worth, is lacklustre. spoilers ahead. the main game is built off of the foundation of Ao Oni version 6.23, also known as the final version of the rpgmaker classic. this means that all puzzles are identical to the original game. if you've played it once, you're better off playing the original rpgmaker version instead. -while i like the new dialogue sprites, with mika being my favourite, the over world sprites feel extremely out of place and strangely cuter compared to 6.23. the oni sprites were barely changed, save for some alterations that just make him look grossly smooth. -the movement is also extremely slippery, with you easily moving way more fast than you want to. this applies to pushing objects too, where instead of having to press enter to move something, you just slide it along effortlessly. -when i tried to save, i was immediately introduced to the strange menu sounds. it gets extremely grating at some points, but eventually you do get numb to the assault on your ears. -some of the random encounters are quite odd. a few of them (more notably, the Mika-o Oni chase which happened in the basement of the old building of my playthrough) gave you barely any time to react. the fuwatti chase as well is strangely more difficult. i can relatively handle the original fuwatti encounter in 6.23, but for some reason he's way more hard to deal with in this remaster. -the Ao Oni remaster also took one step forward and two steps back in my eyes in terms of the notable cut-scenes. while the new mika scream was actually really chilling, the jail-cell scene was completely ruined, with it being shortened and being accompanied with a silly dramatic sting than deafening silence. the post credits scene too was turned from, admittedly, quite interesting to a laughing stock. the Ao Onis thermal vision being replaced by a bog standard inverted effect, and the scream being changed (for to my knowledge, no reason) to the flapjack scream? -the oni doesn't fake you out anymore, and you can't even *choose* to leave the closet early until your heart rate decreases. it feels exactly like the mobile games. i *would* try the new campaign -Ai's Story-, i already don't want to touch this game again. TL;DR - this is an Ao NO-ni from me dawg

This is probably one of the most disappointing remakes I've played, and for a game I have very fond memories of, it hurts. Let's go over the positives first) - Each item how having its own image is nice - The new graphic for entering a closet is pretty cool - Pushing around chairs is faster - Mika's scream is better? Ok, the bad) - The animations for Hiroshi look so goofy walking around - The new tile assets for the mansion look worse than the original, especially in parts like the Annex, where everything is brighter and takes away from the original darker aesthetic - The portraits for the characters take away from the sort of 'Junji Ito' style the original had - The sprites for the characters look like they were overcompensating for nothing - There are points where you can trigger story sequences while still being chased by an Oni - The new Ai game mode is just a randomizer that you can knock out in like 5 or 6 minutes It's honestly just disappointing because we've seen good remakes of RPGMaker horror games like Ib and The Witch's House that understand what made the original special. You want to play Ao Oni? The original is better, and it's completely free

[b]Overall Rating[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Story[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Gameplay[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Graphics[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Soundtrack[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Sound Design[/b] [h1]★★☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Difficulty[/b] [h1]★★★★☆[/h1] [b]Bug free ?[/b] [h1]★★★★★[/h1] [b]PC Requirements[/b] [h1]★☆☆☆☆[/h1] [b]Replay Value[/b] [h1]★★☆☆☆[/h1] [h1]Not Recommended - ✘[/h1] My concept : Doing an indie RPG marathon and reviewing already known or totally unknown games ! This time i decided to test and review “Ao Oni” which is a game I never wanted to try out more younger because of the visuals of it and also because it never did interested me even a little at all to be honest... Ao Oni is a product of its time. It was one of the games that caused this big boom of RPG Maker Horror Games that came about in the 2000s, It was a big hit at his time even more in Japan. That being said, we’re over a decade past Ao Oni’s conception, and while I knew about Ao Oni for so long, my first time playing was only recently because I grew up and I said to myself : damn, it was very popular back in the day, there must be a reason for it ! So curiosity did win over my reluctant thoughts and I tried the game : now review time ! Ao oni is a freeware indie game made with RPG Maker XP. In it, you take control of a high schooler named Hiroshi who, along with three other friends, decides to explore an abandoned mansion on the outskirts of town that is said to be haunted. Your goal is to move Hiroshi through a series of 2D, top down rooms (rendered in typical 16 bit fashion) exploring the mansion and trying to find a way to escape after something traps you inside. In this sense, Ao Oni plays pretty much like standard horror adventure/puzzle game involving gathering items, solving logic puzzles, finding clues, backtracking with keys, and all those traditional elements. However, there’s a bit more to it than that : as you make your way through the mansion, you’re constantly being stalked by the titular Ao Oni and it’s this simple addition that makes Ao Oni one… tense game to play or like I prefer to say a frankly frustrating game to play at some point. The mechanics of Ao Oni‘s antagonist are rather simple, and this is what makes him so surprising and as the same time so goofy. He appears at both random and preset points during your exploration of the game ( by preset, I mean he’ll appear after you solve a puzzle or find a clue, like Nemesis from Resident Evil 3 and by random, I mean that he can literally ambush you as you move between rooms randomly ) and proceeds to chase you around the house. You can’t fight against him, so if he catches Hiroshi, it means instant death and Game Over and here come the reason why I call the play style of this game to be as tense as frustrating. When he appears, you have no choice but to run away from him and try to lose him (by evading him for a specific amount of time depending on the difficulty you chosen) or by hiding in certain places around the mansion. The Oni can appear at any time and from any direction, and often you’re given no warning as to when he’s about to come and try to eat you. This element of the game creates a lot of tension, as you find yourself surprised at any random movement, trying to anticipate the Oni’s arrival and, when he appears, the game turns into a kinda stressful experience as first. But sadly we got used to the feeling of his arrival and we can preshot it pretty easily. It can become easily annoying when you get cornered and stuck in some room without any possibilities than playing with the save files to come back to previous ones. If you’re looking for anything other than a challenge and some surprise though, Ao Oni doesn’t have much to offer. This is a game that is designed to provide the gamer with two things : surprise and puzzle based gameplay. The story of Ao Oni isn’t something that ever takes centre stage which is funny when you think about this game got movies, mangas and anime adaptations. The reason for your character and his friends entering the mansion is never revealed, and nor are the origins of the Oni. There isn’t any attempt at characterisation or expanding on any of the characters personalities or motives, which makes it impossible to feel anything for any of your companions. In terms of graphics and sound, Ao Oni does a competent job. Due to the fact that this is an RPG Maker game, the environments are all rendered in basic 2D sprite based graphics. They do well enough to the degree that you know what everything is meant to be and where you are, but the art style in general appears to be very minimalistic, and the mansion is nowhere near as detailed as some other RPG Maker games can be. The sound is also handled in a minimalistic way, with the only sounds you’ll hear in the game being the pouring rain outside the house and a dramatic series of chords when the Oni attacks. There isn’t anything particularly memorable but this isn’t necessarily a bad thing. Instead, the use of silence actually helps to emphasise the game’s feeling of isolation in a way and hearing scary music suddenly play when your stalker appears has sufficient surprise effect even if the chassing theme become also super boring after some time. The silent ambiance of the game definitely made me umconfortable and if it was the intention, congrats and well done ! Some puzzle where good but most of them were weirdly designed. There’s a sliding block puzzle about halfway through the game, and you’d imagine you’d have to solve it right? Wrong, it’s a red herring, and you have to do a full sequence of puzzles to get the head off one doll, and just put the head in the slot of the sliding block puzzle. This is just not intuitive at all and definitely without a guide I wouldn’t have guessed this one. To be honest the only interesting part of the game is the blue oni that honestly has one of the worst design of monster I’ve ever saw ( special mention to the yandere dev ao oni meme ). The Oni design is just so much funnier than it is scary. Playing this, I just couldn't help but laugh whenever seeing the oni. This is even more true with the other Oni designs that are seen later in the game. I still remember this moment back when I played this with my boyfriend for the first time, I was following a guide and it was near end of the game. The guide described a scripted monster chase, with a new type of Oni described as “the scariest thing ever”, and when the scripted sequence started, we were laughing our heads off because that Oni’s design was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ goofy. I forgot to talk about the side little game called Ai's Story with this random girl with white hair named Ai ( Ao and Ai, that was a lot of research for the name xD ) that you could play after finishing the main game but basically you can finish it in maximum ten minutes and it just consists of randomized rooms where you need to find items to escape : end of the game. So is it worth buying Ao Oni on steam for this little add on ? Definitely no. And I’m not even talking about how you’re supposed to have 100% achievements on this game on steam. The system of rank is just painful since if you want to have a S rank you need to always save and load every time you die to have a count of zero deaths at the end and you need to not waste time on puzzle so you can finish fast enough to succeed… a pleasure, definitely a pleasure… Basically, learn the whole game to do it fast and never die to have all achievements ! That's cool, not at all unmotivating ! I think this game is only so iconic because of the goofy design of Ao Oni. He isn't scary and the story doesn't exist so the game doesn't do much to stand out, I was expecting much more because of how popular this game is. Please don’t inflict this experience on yourself and go play some good indie horror rpg like Mad Father, Omori or IB.

It's basically the Ao Oni version 6.23 (the one that's free and avaiable), but on Steam and paid. You'd think they'd add something substantial for this to have 10$ price tag globally, but the only added things are the Ai's story (maze made up from randomly selected rooms from the game) and the increased speed gamemodes. That's it. You can also notice the updated artstyle, this is partly because the game is partly based on the mobile Ao Oni games, the core feature of those were selectable Ao Oni skins. Are they in this? NO. More invested Ao Oni players know that the game changed significantly between versions. Are those older game versions playable in this? Also no. Are there even any changes to the game beyond the engine and graphics? Yes, the chances for non-scripted chases has been increased to the point you are nigh always chased (and you will be chased way more due to random encounters rather than the scripted, puzzle solving ones), ruinning the suspence and atmosphere. Just get the old free version(s)
